name: The Defias Brotherhood
summary: In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood is building a network beyond banditry. Wiley the Black sends word of its ties to gnolls, kobolds, and goblins. Gryan Stoutmantle needs this intelligence to measure the full reach of the conspiracy choking Westfall.

sections.title: A Dangerous Dispatch
sections.body: Wiley the Black says telling what he knows about the Defias could cost him his life. Along the edges of Redridge and Westfall, he has caught wind of an operation far greater than highway robbery. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups that are usually hostile to one another across the countryside.

sections.title: Unlikely Alliances
sections.body: Wiley warns that the Defias has drawn an alarming network around itself. The red-masked outlaws have enlisted gnoll packs, kobold diggers, and goblin engineers instead of working alone. Together, their brutal muscle, burrowing labor, and mechanical cunning point to an enterprise beyond what the People's Militia first expected.

sections.title: Stoutmantle's Uneasy Reliance
sections.body: Gryan Stoutmantle has little love for Wiley and openly laments that he did not leave the rogue to rot when he had the chance. Yet Westfall cannot afford pride. With Stormwind ignoring pleas for military aid, the People's Militia must take useful intelligence wherever it can find it.

faq.answer: Wiley the Black's note warns that the Defias Brotherhood is coordinating with gnolls, kobolds, and goblin engineers. It tells the People's Militia that the outlaws are preparing an operation far beyond petty banditry.

Wiley the Black is a shady contact stationed at Lakeshire in Redridge. Gryan Stoutmantle sees him as an untrustworthy scoundrel, but Wiley has extensive ties to the criminal underworld and critical information on Defias activity.

faq.q: Why would the Defias ally with gnolls and kobolds?
faq.answer: The Defias uses local creatures to control territory and provide cheap labor. Gnolls serve as brutish skirmishers to distract defenders, kobolds tunnel in regional mines, and goblin tinkers contribute heavy machinery and demolition tools.

faq.q: Why does Gryan Stoutmantle dislike Wiley?
faq.answer: Gryan Stoutmantle is a disciplined former soldier who sees Wiley as a common cutpurse and criminal. He regrets sparing Wiley from prison, though Wiley's underworld ears are indispensable.

faq.q: Where does this message fit into the militia's investigation?
faq.answer: Wiley's message carries the militia's investigation from local reconnaissance toward the deeper Defias conspiracy. Its return prompts Stoutmantle to probe the conspiracy's leadership and staging grounds.

faq.q: Why isn't Stormwind handling this threat?
faq.answer: With King Varian Wrynn missing, the Stormwind House of Nobles refuses to divert royal soldiers or funding to defend Westfall. Stoutmantle's ragtag People's Militia is left to defend the region.

angles.text: For the Alliance, coordination between human outlaws, gnolls, and goblins shows the severe security vacuum on Stormwind's western borders.
As a rogue, you can see how Wiley the Black walks the line between outlaw and useful informant, and how underworld ties carry wartime intelligence.
As a human, you know the note confirms that bandits pillaging family homesteads in Westfall and Redridge are carrying out a deliberate, coordinated campaign.
